title: TEG / ROTEM Interpretation
sources: Critical Vector — TEG Interpretation: A Complete Teaching Guide (TEG 5000 + TEG 6s + ROTEM crosswalk)
Whiting D, DiNardo JA. TEG and ROTEM: technology and clinical applications. Am J Hematol 2014;89(2):228-232
Einersen PM et al. Rapid TEG thresholds for goal-directed resuscitation. J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2017;82(1):114-119
Robson JL et al. Correlation between TEG 5000 and TEG 6s during liver transplant. Anaesth Intensive Care 2019;47(2):124-131

changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from the CV TEG teaching guide: raw tracing, TEG 5000 parameters, TEG 6s channels, platelet mapping, the 5000↔6s↔ROTEM crosswalk, goal-directed framework, tracing-by-shape, pitfalls, special populations.

summary: Viscoelastic testing measures the physical strength of a clot as it forms, matures, and breaks down in whole blood — enabling product-specific, goal-directed transfusion instead of empiric 1:1:1 ratios. Treat the parameter that is actually abnormal.

body.text: Every parameter is a labeled point on one spindle-shaped curve: R = time to initial clot formation · K = time to a fixed early amplitude · α (alpha angle) = slope of the widening curve · MA = peak width, i.e. clot strength · LY30 = amplitude lost 30 min after MA.
TEG 5000 — the classic five (single kaolin-activated channel)

rows: Sample run → initial fibrin (1–2 mm amplitude)
Slope of the widening tracing — speed of fibrin accumulation

body.text: Trauma-specific thresholds refine these: R time beyond ~ 2× normal predicts massive-transfusion need, and LY30 > 3% in the injured patient (a lower bar than the general reference range) identifies clinically significant hyperfibrinolysis warranting an antifibrinolytic. Myth: alpha angle is NOT a pure fibrinogen measure — on the TEG 5000 alone, isolated fibrinogen deficiency cannot be cleanly separated from platelet dysfunction. That gap is what the TEG 6s functional-fibrinogen channel closes.
TEG 6s — four channels from one draw

rows: Global factor activity; baseline hyperfibrinolysis screen
Rapid overall clot strength when time is critical (massive transfusion)
True factor status with heparin effect removed — compare CK-R vs CKH-R to detect heparin
Kaolin + tissue factor + a GPIIb/IIIa platelet inhibitor
Isolated fibrinogen contribution — MA correlates directly with Clauss fibrinogen

body.text: Standard channels fully activate platelets, so routine MA cannot see aspirin or P2Y12 effect. TEG-PM adds heparinized channels that isolate platelet contribution by agonist. % inhibition = 100 − [(MA_agonist − MA_Fibrin) ÷ (MA_Thrombin − MA_Fibrin) × 100].

rows: P2Y12 receptor — clopidogrel / prasugrel / ticagrelor effect

body.text: Use: perioperative antiplatelet management before neuraxial anesthesia or urgent surgery, identifying clopidogrel non-responders after PCI, guiding platelet transfusion when reversing DAPT for an urgent bleed or ICH.

rows: FIBTEM MCF or A10 (platelets blocked with cytochalasin D)
EXTEM / INTEM MCF (A10 as early surrogate)
EXTEM ML / LI30; APTEM confirms (adds aprotinin)

body.text: Numerical values are NOT interchangeable between platforms — head-to-head comparison in liver transplant found considerable inter-device variability. Trend a patient on one platform; do not convert a TEG 5000 result to a TEG 6s or ROTEM threshold. APTEM is the one ROTEM assay with no TEG analog: if adding an antifibrinolytic normalizes an abnormal EXTEM, that confirms hyperfibrinolysis and supports giving TXA.

rows: FFP, or PCC if rapid correction needed
Protamine (patient-specific) rather than more factor product
K prolonged / alpha low / CFF-MA low
Cryoprecipitate, or fibrinogen concentrate where available
TXA or aminocaproic acid — NOT more factor or platelet product
Long flat line before any widening
Prolonged R — factor deficiency or heparin effect
Low alpha / prolonged K — fibrinogen deficiency (confirm with CFF)
Low MA — thrombocytopenia or platelet dysfunction
Wide spindle that narrows sharply after the peak
Wide spindle, slow to narrow, persists over time
Hypercoagulable state — consider VTE prophylaxis escalation

items: Line/catheter contamination: a heparin flush in the draw falsely prolongs R — discard the first several mL or use a discrete venipuncture.
Sample run outside the validated window: citrate rest-time drift changes R and K — follow the lab's rest-then-run protocol (~ 30 min citrate rest).
Testing at 37 °C in a hypothermic patient masks coagulopathy that is real at the patient's actual temperature.
Anemia / low hematocrit paradoxically inflates MA and lowers alpha angle independent of true platelet or fibrinogen status — interpret MA against the concurrent Hct.
Standard MA cannot distinguish 'too few platelets' from 'platelets present but not working' — correlate with the count or add platelet mapping.

Pregnancy: a physiologic hypercoagulable state — shorter R, steeper alpha, higher MA than non-pregnant ranges. In postpartum hemorrhage, fibrinogen is the first to fall and the strongest single predictor of progression — trend CFF-MA / FIBTEM rather than waiting on standard coags.

Cirrhosis: INR and platelet count overstate bleeding risk (they ignore the parallel loss of protein C/S and elevated vWF that rebalance hemostasis at a lower set point). TEG/ROTEM reflect this and reduce unnecessary pre-procedure FFP — but neither reliably captures the qualitative platelet defects or portal-hypertension hyperfibrinolysis of advanced disease.
Pediatric / neonatal: developmental hemostasis shifts normal ranges with age — use age-specific reference ranges, not adult cutoffs.
